abstract: Users cannot reliably translate their creative intents into AI-generated music. We contend that the root of this difficulty lies in associative divergence: associations between narratives and musical features are overly remote, and users lack a visible mediation structure to negotiate them. To address this, we introduce five core schema groups as cognitive mediation and propose a bidirectional schema-based framework. Its forward pathway decomposes narrative-to-music associations into staged mappings, while its reverse pathway provides structured interpretations from music back to narrative. Findings from two user studies(N = 188; N = 60) show that the framework led to clearer creative expression and greater perceived control, improved the comprehensibility of generated music, especially for unconventional pieces. Furthermore, it supported cultural and affective thinking while helping users locate associative divergence. Our work points toward better creative intent alignment in human-AI music co-creation.

ur.ai_reason: 人机音乐共创，含两项用户研究
ur.tldr: 针对用户难以将叙事意图转化为AI音乐的关联偏差，构建双向模式框架，将叙事—音乐映射分阶段展开，并支持从音乐反向解释叙事。两项用户研究显示其能提升创意表达、掌控感与音乐可理解性。

title: Decomposing the Associative Chain: Schema-Based Mediation Supports Expression and Understanding in Human-AI Music Co-creation
title_zh: 解构联想链：基于图式的中介支持人机音乐共创中的表达与理解
